title: [WT-10P] Proxy: preserve bounded blocking replies after one-shot stdin EOF
description:
Objective: make wrapper-issued wait_for_resource usable through the actual one-shot moe-proxy transport before WT-10 relies on it. Verified source defect: scripts/moe-agent.sh moe_rpc and PS Invoke-MoeRpc pipe one request then close stdin; packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts gracefulShutdown uses a flat 2000ms drain, so queued blocking requests are cancelled long before their own timeout. Existing memory mem:gotcha-moe-proxy-oneshot-kills-blocking-longpolls confirms real-daemon reproduction.
Deliverable: bounded EOF-drain handling for known blocking wait_for_resource/wait_for_task/chat_wait requests using their recorded request deadlines. Keep explicit SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown promptly bounded, ordinary-request/empty EOF behavior unchanged, no indefinite reconnect/wait, and deterministic error responses when the request cannot finish. Regression coverage in packages/moe-proxy/src/index.test.ts with the real spawned proxy and fake WS server; inspect existing pendingRequestTimes/getRequestTimeout and shutdown tests before planning. Expected edited files: src/index.ts and src/index.test.ts; avoid wrapper-specific stdin-holding workarounds.
NOT in scope: caller identity, task state, lease semantics, changing daemon tool contracts or installing/restarting the live fleet. WT-10 must use a proxy built from this fix; packaged rollout is owned by epic hardening.
Verification from repo root: (cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test) && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh. Regression tests must spawn compiled current source, not stale dist.
definitionOfDone: A real proxy receiving a known blocking tools/call followed by stdin EOF returns a delayed valid daemon response after more than 2 seconds instead of Proxy shutting down before response received; the test fails on current source.
A blocked request with no daemon response exits within its recorded finite deadline and emits a truthful error; unavailable/disconnected daemon and queued-unsent requests do not hang indefinitely.
SIGINT/SIGTERM remain promptly bounded even while an EOF-drain is pending, and all timeout/connection/process cleanup executes without duplicate responses or leaked children.
Ordinary requests and no-pending-request EOF retain existing shutdown behavior, demonstrated by unchanged existing tests.
The exact verification command exits 0 and the current proxy build is the binary under test.

implementationPlan.description:
EOF drain for one-shot blocking calls, plus its tests (packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts, src/index.test.ts).

Blast-radius rule: every agent CLI talks MCP through this proxy, and an MCP client always sends `initialize` first. The wrapper one-shots never do: moe_rpc, Invoke-MoeRpc and moe-call.sh pipe one bare tools/call, then close stdin. So the long drain applies ONLY to a session that never sent `initialize`. An exiting CLI's proxy must not linger for up to 11 minutes holding a parked wait_for_task or chat_wait.

index.ts changes:
- Track `sawInitialize`: true once any stdin message, or any batch element, has method 'initialize'.
- Add `isBlockingLongPoll(parsed)`, which getRequestTimeout reuses. Give each pendingRequestTimes entry a `blocking` flag at BOTH places entries are created: the stdin send path and the ws 'open' flush of queued messages.
- `BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS = parsePositiveIntEnv(process.env.MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS, 11 * 60 * 1000)` replaces WAIT_FOR_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS. The default is unchanged; tests need the knob.
- Replace gracefulShutdown with `gracefulShutdown(cause: 'eof' | 'signal')`:
  - A signal sets `signalCapAt = min(signalCapAt, now + 2000)`.
  - A repeat call returns once the cap is recorded, so the old stacked intervals are gone.
  - The first call keeps today's prologue: shuttingDown, clear the reconnect timer, stop the timeout checker, and exit 0 at once when nothing is pending. It then starts ONE 50ms drain interval.
- Each drain tick:
  - A sent pending id's deadline is `sentAt + timeoutMs` when cause is 'eof', !sawInitialize and it is blocking. It becomes `now` when that blocking request's socket is gone (currentWebSocket null: ws 'close' returns early during shutdown and emits nothing). Every other id gets `shutdownStartedAt + 2000`, today's flat grace. All deadlines are capped by signalCapAt and step 2's absolute deadline.
  - Queued (unsent) messages keep the flat 2000ms. A queued blocking request flushed by a late 'open' gets its own deadline from then on.
  - Due ids are removed from pendingRequestIds, pendingRequestTimes and pendingToolsListIds BEFORE their one error is written, so the existing unknown-id guard drops any late daemon reply.
  - Error texts: `Request timed out after <timeoutMs>ms` for a blocking request past its deadline; 'Connection to daemon lost before response received' when its socket is gone; the unchanged 'Proxy shutting down before response received' and 'Proxy shutting down with message still queued' for the grace and signal paths.
  - With nothing left: closeWebSocket() and exit 0.
- stdin 'end'/'error' call gracefulShutdown('eof'); SIGTERM/SIGINT call gracefulShutdown('signal').

Error handling: every request id gets exactly one response; there is never a reconnect during shutdown, an unbounded wait, or a duplicate line; stdout EPIPE still exits through safeStdoutWrite.

Tests use the existing spawned `node dist/index.js` and mock WebSocketServer, and measure times from stdin EOF:
- T1 (DoD 1): a bare tools/call moe.wait_for_resource with no initialize; the server replies after 3000ms; write then end() at once. Expect exactly one stdout line, a result for id 1, arriving >=2500ms after EOF, and exit 0. This fails on current source.
- T2 (DoD 2): MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 and the server never replies. Expect one 'Request timed out after 3000ms' for id 1 between ~2.5s and 6s, and exit 0.
- T3 (DoD 2): the server terminates the socket 1s after the blocking request arrives. Expect one 'Connection to daemon lost before response received' within ~1.5s of that, and exit.
- T4 (DoD 2): daemon.json names a port with no listener, so the request stays queued. Expect one 'Proxy shutting down with message still queued' within ~3s, and exit.
- T5 (DoD 3), it.each over SIGTERM and SIGINT, `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`: the server replies after 10s; end(), then the signal 500ms later. Expect one 'Proxy shutting down before response received' for id 1, exit within 2.5s of the signal, and no second line for id 1.
- T6 (DoD 4): (a) an initialized session (initialize answered, then a blocking call the server answers after 3000ms) still errors at the ~2s grace; (b) a one-shot ordinary tools/list with no reply errors at ~2s.
Every existing test passes unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: EOF drain: gracefulShutdown(cause) + drainVerdict/drainTick; trackRequest/forgetRequest used at both tracking sites (stdin send + ws 'open' flush) with a blocking flag; sawInitialize gate; BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS from MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS (default 11 min). 9 new spawned-proxy tests (T1 x2 after/before connect, T2, T3, T4, T5 x2 SIGTERM/SIGINT skipIf win32, T6a, T6b). RED on HEAD source: T1x2, T2, T3 failed (2s 'Proxy shutting down before response received'); GREEN after fix: src/index.test.ts 24/24 in Linux snapshot /tmp/moe-b5a1-gate.5lj7Mx (native node_modules hardlinked from a lock-matching tree; shared checkout node_modules is Windows-only). Drain does not itself cap at the absolute deadline: step 2's timer fires at its own time, so the earlier bound wins. Shared-checkout dirty paths from other sessions untouched.

MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS: parseOneShotDeadline (blank=unset; strict /^[0-9]+$/ + Number.isSafeInteger; invalid -> one null-id 'Invalid MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS: <reason>' with the value JSON-escaped and capped at 64 chars, exit 1 before connect()); armDeadline re-arms in 2^31-1 ms steps because setTimeout clamps longer delays to 1ms (a far-future deadline would otherwise fire at once); expireDeadline sets shuttingDown, clears reconnect/drain/timeout timers, forgets ids then writes one 'Proxy deadline exceeded (MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS)' per sent+queued id (null-id when none known), exit 1. Timer kept ref'd so the bound always fires. Tests: never-connected (1.5s, null-id, exit 1), waiting (2.5s cuts a 4s reply, exit 1, no late result), invalid it.each x5 (abc, -5, 1e12, 20 nines, 5000-char) fail closed with no ws connection and <200-char message, blank + 40-days-away leave a normal call alone. src/index.test.ts 33/33 in snapshot; mutation probe removing the re-arm makes the 40-days test fail.

implementationPlan.description:
Docs and test isolation (packages/moe-proxy/README.md, packages/moe-proxy/vitest.config.ts).
- README 'Environment Variables', two entries:
  - `MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS`: wrapper-only. An absolute Unix-epoch-ms bound for one call; blank means unset; any other invalid value fails closed (exit 1). At expiry, one error per pending id, then exit 1.
  - `MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS`: the per-request deadline of moe.wait_for_task, moe.chat_wait and moe.wait_for_resource, default 660000.
- A short 'One-shot calls' section: in a session that never sent `initialize`, stdin EOF lets a pending blocking call finish up to its deadline. Initialized MCP sessions and ordinary calls keep the 2-second drain, and SIGINT/SIGTERM cap any drain at 2 seconds.
- vitest.config.ts: add 'MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS' and 'MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS' to the blanked env list, so no developer or seat env leaks into a spawned test proxy (blank = unset, as for the other names).
implementationPlan.note: README: env entries for MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS (default 660000) and MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS (wrapper-only, blank=unset, invalid fails closed), plus a 'One-shot calls' section (initialize gate, lost-socket fail-fast, 2s drain for initialized/ordinary/queued, signal cap, deadline expiry semantics). vitest.config.ts blanks both new env names. SCOPE GROWTH (one extra docs file): docs/CONFIGURATION.md 'Proxy Configuration' table is the repo's env-var reference and already lists every proxy env (MOE_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS etc.), so two rows were added there to keep it complete; no daemon doc-contract test (executionContractDocs/daemonGitDocs/taskTimeBudgetDocs) asserts on those rows.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review, the final step. Load adversarial-self-review and attack this diff:
1. Can any request id get zero or two responses? Check the drain racing a late daemon reply, ws 'close' during shutdown, the deadline timer racing the drain, and a signal racing EOF.
2. Can an initialized CLI session ever wait past 2s at EOF?
3. Can a one-shot blocking call wait past min(its deadline, the absolute deadline, signal + 2s)?
4. Does any timer, interval or socket outlive process.exit, or leak in tests?
5. Does a queued message flushed by a late 'open' carry the right blocking flag and deadline?
6. Error handling: is an invalid or blank env value handled exactly as documented, and is the env value never echoed unbounded?
7. Are the timing assertions robust on a slow CI box? Use generous upper bounds and strict lower bounds only where the DoD needs them (>2s).
8. Do all pre-existing tests pass unchanged?
If any byte changes, re-run step 4's command and submit that output.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review of git diff HEAD -- packages/moe-proxy docs/CONFIGURATION.md. FIXED: expiry docs/comment said null-id error 'when none is known'; actual behavior is 'when none is pending' (also fires if every request was already answered while stdin stays open) - wording corrected in index.ts comment, README, CONFIGURATION.md (no logic change). Checked: (1) one response per id - drain and expireDeadline forget ids before writing, the unknown-id guard drops late replies, ws 'close' returns early while shuttingDown, a repeat gracefulShutdown only tightens signalCapAt, expireDeadline exits synchronously; (2) sawInitialize forces the 2s grace for every id, queued msgs always use the grace; (3) waits bounded by min(sentAt+timeoutMs, signal+2s) in the drain (+<=50ms tick) and the absolute timer fires on its own; (4) process.exit ends all timers; tests clear reply timers and SIGKILL leftover children in afterEach; (5) flush path covered by a mutation probe; (6) blank=unset, ' 123' / '1e12' / '-5' / 20 digits fail closed, value JSON-escaped and capped at 64 chars; (7) strict lower bounds only where the DoD needs >2s, generous upper bounds; (8) pre-existing tests untouched and pass. comments.content: Consumer contract needed by WT-10's hard overall MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC bound: add an opt-in per-process absolute deadline environment variable MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS (integer Unix epoch milliseconds, set only for a wrapper one-shot resource RPC). It must bound startup/connect/queued-unsent/sent/EOF-drain together; at expiry emit a non-success response for known pending IDs and exit, with no late success or reconnect. Missing env leaves all existing behavior intact; invalid supplied values fail closed rather than disable the bound. Explicit signals still shut down promptly. Test both waiting and never-connected proxy, including a short deadline, and document this wrapper-only env in packages/moe-proxy/README.md (third file). This is a new producer contract, not an already-existent helper. WT-10 will pass the remaining overall deadline on each acquire/wait call and a short independent cleanup deadline for release, avoiding duplicated Python/.NET process-supervision code or shell-specific timeout binaries.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: In a proxy session that never sent the MCP `initialize`, which is a wrapper one-shot RPC, stdin EOF no longer cancels a pending moe.wait_for_task, moe.chat_wait or moe.wait_for_resource after 2s. Each such call drains until its daemon reply or its recorded deadline (sentAt + MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS, default 11 min), and fails at once if the daemon socket is lost. Ordinary calls, queued-unsent messages and every initialized MCP session keep today's 2s drain. SIGINT/SIGTERM cap any drain at 2s. The opt-in MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS bounds the whole process: at expiry it writes one error per known id (a null-id error before any id is known) and exits 1. A blank value means unset, and any other invalid value fails closed. Every request id gets exactly one response.
acceptanceCriteria: A one-shot blocking call with EOF returns a daemon reply that arrives after >2s; the test fails on current source.
A one-shot blocking call with no reply errors within its recorded deadline; a lost socket, a never-opened socket and queued-unsent messages never hang.
SIGINT/SIGTERM during an EOF drain exit within 2s with exactly one response per id.
Ordinary requests, no-pending EOF and initialized sessions keep the 2s behavior; existing tests pass unchanged.
MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS bounds never-connected and waiting proxies (exit 1, no late success); invalid values fail closed.
`(cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test)` plus parity-check on a HEAD snapshot exits 0 against a freshly built dist.
invariants: Exactly one response per request id; no reconnect after shutdown starts.
An initialized (CLI) session never waits more than 2s after stdin EOF.
No env value is echoed unbounded to stdout.
compatibility: Existing stdout error texts are unchanged for the grace, queued and disconnect paths.
Unset or blank env vars leave all prior behavior intact.
Wrapper callers (moe_rpc, Invoke-MoeRpc, moe-call.sh) need no change to benefit.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- (1) Use each request's own timeout for every EOF, as the memory gotcha-moe-proxy-oneshot-kills-blocking-longpolls suggested. Rejected as stated: every exiting CLI with a parked chat_wait or wait_for_task would leave its proxy alive for up to 11 minutes, holding a daemon long-poll for a dead session. The `initialize` handshake is the protocol-level discriminator: MCP clients always send it, and wrapper one-shots never do.
- (2) The wrappers hold stdin open instead. Rejected: the task forbids wrapper-specific stdin workarounds, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 has no clean equivalent.
- (3) Derive the blocking deadline from the call's own timeoutMs argument. Rejected: it couples the proxy to three daemon schemas; the daemon answers at its own timeout anyway, which is always under the 11-minute tier.
- (4) No absolute deadline. Rejected: WT-10 (comment-8b75fe92) needs one bound over connect, queue and drain, and without it would duplicate per-shell process supervision.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts:
  - gracefulShutdown (~L314) is a flat 2000ms wait polled every 50ms, then errors every pending id and exits 0; it is called from stdin end/error AND SIGTERM/SIGINT, and today stacks a second interval when called twice.
  - The stdin reader is installed in openDaemonSocket (~L555), so a one-shot request written before the socket opens is queued in pendingMessages and flushed by ws 'open' (~L424), even during shutdown.
  - ws 'close' returns early while shuttingDown (~L500), leaving emission to the drain.
  - checkMessageTimeouts is skipped while shuttingDown.
  - The unknown-id guard in ws 'message' drops late replies.
  - getRequestTimeout returns the 11-minute tier for BLOCKING_LONG_POLLS.
- index.ts runs main() at import, so tests drive the spawned dist (index.test.ts spawns `node ../dist/index.js`; `npm test`'s pretest rebuilds it).
- vitest.config.ts blanks MOE_* env for spawned proxies.
- moe_rpc (scripts/moe-agent.sh) does `echo "$rpc" | proxy || return 1`: a single bare tools/call, id 1, no initialize.
planningNotes.risks:
- Timing tests on slow CI: keep lower bounds only where the DoD needs them (>2s); give upper bounds generous slack.
- Signals on Windows: node kill() has no handler semantics, so skip the signal tests on win32.
- The ws 'open' flush during shutdown must set the blocking flag, or a queued one-shot call would fall back to 2s, which is the very bug.
- Never echo the raw env value unbounded into stdout.
- The fleet only gets this proxy through a rebuild or plugin reinstall; WT-10 tests must use the built source, and epic hardening owns rollout.

completionSummary: moe-proxy EOF drain for one-shot blocking calls + opt-in absolute deadline (packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts). In a session that never sent `initialize` (the wrappers' moe_rpc / Invoke-MoeRpc / moe-call.sh), stdin EOF no longer cuts a pending moe.wait_for_task / chat_wait / wait_for_resource at 2s. It drains to sentAt + MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS (default 660000, unchanged) and gives `Request timed out after <n>ms`, or fails at once with the existing disconnect text if the socket drops. Initialized CLI sessions, ordinary calls and queued messages keep the 2s drain with unchanged texts. SIGINT/SIGTERM cap any drain at 2s, and a repeat shutdown call only tightens that cap; the old code stacked a second interval. Both tracking sites (stdin send, ws 'open' flush) record the blocking flag through trackRequest. MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS (epoch ms) bounds the whole process: one 'Proxy deadline exceeded' error per pending id, or one null-id error when none is pending, then exit 1. Blank means unset. Invalid values fail closed (null-id error, value escaped and capped at 64 chars, exit 1, no connect). Far deadlines re-arm past setTimeout's 2^31-1 clamp. Tests: 18 new spawned-proxy cases in src/index.test.ts. RED on HEAD: 4 tests failed (2s cut). Mutation probes confirm the flush-path and timer-overflow tests have teeth. Docs: README env entries and a One-shot calls section; vitest.config blanks both env names. Two CONFIGURATION.md rows are a docs scope addition noted in step 3.
